extractions.description: A position/critique paper arguing that AI scaling laws rely on evaluation metrics that may not reflect the values of the many subpopulations represented in ever-larger datasets. Drawing on machine learning and social science literature, the authors argue that as dataset size grows, the number of communities with potentially incompatible values and metrics grows, threatening the validity of claims that model performance improves at scale. No experiments are run.

type.quote: We draw on literature from the social sciences and machine learning to critically interrogate these claims.
